settings_marks_the_block_you_are: Marks the block you are in, and the block at the same place in every reference open beside it — so you can see which paragraph or poetry line answers which.
settings_typing_1_1_v1_or: Typing "1", "1.", "v1" or "verse 1" and then a space starts that verse, when it is the next verse or within the reference's count for the chapter, and never one the chapter already has. Pasted text follows the same rule, and Backspace just after a verse's number turns it back into the number. Turn this off to keep such numbers as words.
settings_in_refine_this_many_spaces: In Refine, this many spaces typed at the start of a line make it a poetry line, or move it one level in, as Tab does. Off, spaces are only spaces.

sous_setting_placement_description: Flags a punctuation mark or digit right next to something it is rarely next to in this project, like a comma touching the next word, by counting every use of that mark across the whole project.
sous_setting_run_shape_description: Flags a group of marks written together, like “;'”, when this project rarely groups that mark that way and does not write that exact group often.
sous_setting_exact_neighbor_description: Flags two marks side by side, like “?,”, when this project almost never puts the second one right after the first.
sous_setting_pooled_neighbor: A mark and the kind of mark after it
sous_setting_pooled_neighbor_description: Flags a mark followed directly by a kind of mark, such as a quotation mark or a dash, that rarely follows it in this project; off by default because the pairs check already covers it.
sous_setting_rarity_description: Lists characters this project uses only a handful of times in all its books, like a curly apostrophe in a project that otherwise uses straight ones.
sous_setting_casing_description: Flags a word capitalized, or not, in a way this project rarely writes that word in the middle of a sentence, like “On” where the project writes “on”.
sous_setting_terminal_upper_share_bp_des: How often this project must follow a mark with a capital before a capital there counts as the mark's doing and not the word's.
sous_setting_terminal_lower_share_bp_des: How rarely a mark may be followed by a capital for a capital after it to be checked; marks between this and the capital setting are left alone.
sous_setting_sentence_start_description: Flags a lowercase word right after a mark, like “?” or “!”, that this project almost always follows with a capital.
sous_setting_sentence_start_upper_bp_des: How often this project must follow a mark with a capital before a lowercase word after that mark is flagged.
sous_setting_word_length_description: Flags words far longer than the words this project usually uses, which can mean two words ran together; off by default because long names are common.
sous_setting_word_length_sigma: How long a very long word is
sous_setting_word_length_sigma_descripti: How far past this project's usual word length a word must be, counted in steps of how much word lengths usually vary, before the long-word check flags it.
sous_setting_doubled_description: Turns every check for a word written twice in a row on or off.
sous_setting_doubled_bare_description: Flags a word written twice in a row with only a space between, like “the the”, unless this project does that with the word often.
sous_setting_doubled_separated_descripti: Flags a word written twice with punctuation between, like “Moses, Moses”, unless this project does that with the word often; off by default because calling someone by name twice is common.
sous_setting_doubles_productive_bp_descr: When more than this share of the different words in the project are written twice in a row more than once, the project is taken to repeat words on purpose and the doubled-word checks stay silent.
sous_setting_letter_runs_description: Flags a letter written more times in a row than this project ever writes it, like “joyfullly”.
sous_setting_book_rate_description: Flags one book that puts a mark next to something far more often than the project's other books do, like a dash after a space in one book only.
sous_setting_book_rate_ratio: One book: how many times more
sous_setting_book_rate_ratio_description: How many times more often than the other books typically do one book must put a mark next to something before the one-book check flags it.
sous_setting_book_rate_min_bp_descriptio: The least share of a mark's uses in one book that must be next to the same thing before the one-book check flags that book.
sous_setting_book_rate_min_uses_descript: How many times a book must use a mark before the one-book check may flag that book for it.
sous_setting_lengths_enabled_description: Compares each verse's length with the same verse in the source text and flags verses much longer or shorter than this project usually is.
sous_setting_z_long_description: How far past this project's usual length compared with the source a verse must be, on the long side, before it is flagged as much longer.
sous_setting_z_short_description: How far short of this project's usual length compared with the source a verse must be before it is flagged as much shorter.
sous_setting_min_verses_description: How many verses a book must share with the source before its verse lengths are compared within that book as well as across the project.
sous_setting_presence_description: Flags verses the source text has and this book lacks, verses this book has and the source lacks, and verses left empty.
sous_setting_source_copy_description: Flags words in a row spelled exactly as in the same verse of the source text, which can mean source text was pasted in; off by default.
sous_setting_source_copy_min_run_descrip: How many words in a row must match the source verse before the copied-words check flags them.
sous_setting_support_floor_description: How many times something must occur before the checks treat it as a habit of this project rather than a one-off.
sous_setting_word_support_floor_descript: How many times a word, or a run of one letter, must occur before the capital-letter, long-word and repeated-letter checks compare it with the rest of this project.
tour_triage_verse_numbers_summary: Every verse number out of order, repeated, missing or empty, against your source text, one at a time; each moves on once fixed.
